channel.title: Social Media Today - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Social Media Today (socialmediatoday.com)

item.title: Meta tests shopping AI chatbot in US
item.description: The feature would allow users to request product recommendations, per Bloomberg, and is similar to functions being tested by Google and OpenAI.

item.title: X usage declined in the EU in the second half of 2025
item.description: The platform’s latest reporting showed a decline of nearly 15% since the first half of last year, though the company claims overall record numbers.

item.title: X to take action against AI deepfakes of the Iran war
item.description: Nikita Bier, the platform’s head of product, said users who don’t add AI disclosures will be suspended from Creator Revenue Sharing for at least 90 days.

item.title: Meta updates Edits app with more creation tools
item.description: The company’s development team added video effects and improved the Ideas tab while also bringing in new text elements.

item.title: Snapchat research provides insight for movie marketing
item.description: New data revealed the importance of in-app promotional tools such as influencer recommendations and artificial intelligence suggestions.

item.title: TikTok rules out using end-to-end message encryption
item.description: The app told the BBC that using that level of security would impede police investigations and said stance sets it apart from rivals.

item.title: YouTube updates Payment Activity overview, provides more detailed data
item.description: The platform’s new capabilities include more detailed earnings and payout data to help creators better manage their AdSense accounts.

item.title: TikTok U.S. users impacted by another problem at Oracle
item.description: Problems at a local data center in Ashburn, Virginia, led to more timeouts, errors and latency issues - and user speculation about government interference.

item.title: Snapchat report positions the app as a B2B marketing tool
item.description: New data released in partnership with GWI found that digitally native users are consuming business content outside of traditionally professional online environments.

item.title: xAI considers offering a free version of Grok Enterprise
item.description: The potential rollout would be available to companies with at least 50 employees, with the move suggesting that a paid business plan is on the horizon.
